title: Lower color saturation and perceived luxury brand status
statement:
For luxury branding, lower color saturation increased perceived brand status, with the effect especially apparent below roughly 20–30% saturation, while positioning a luxury brand as innovative reversed the direction and made higher saturation more favorable. (OUP Academic)

Options:
- Heritage muted: 10–20% saturation (fits: timeless, quiet-luxury, heritage)
- Refined middle: 30–40% saturation (fits: premium, balanced, contemporary)
- Visible color: 50–60% saturation (fits: expressive, modern, confident)
- Highly vivid: 70–90% saturation (fits: bold, campaign-led, high-energy)
appliesWhen: Applies to: luxury. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: The Color of Status: Color Saturation, Brand Heritage, and Perceived Status of Luxury Brands
source.authors: Xinyue Zhou; Chunqu Xiao; Sunyee Yoon; Hong Zhu
